note: THE SHORT FLOOR. Nathan, 2026-08-31: 'save everything as the normal floor when making future shorts'. Derived from SANCHEZ_SHORT_FINAL.mp4 - a short he shipped and named as the one that looks right - NOT from the thumbnail floor. A still composite is not footage; solving a short's grade against thumbnail numbers produced the over-processed look he rejected.

OFFERUP_old.verdict: outlier on every axis - bright, flat, undersaturated

captions.entrance_note: machine-readable form of 'entrance' above. tools/short_engine.py and tools/caption_short.py read ENTRANCE from entrance_mode; the engine selftest refuses any value in entrance_rejected (the scale-based entrances he rejected twice on 2026-08-29).
captions.tags_note: fade_ms and blur are the numbers inside 'fade' and 'entrance' above; caption_short._entrance builds \fad(in,out)\blur{px}\t(0,ms,\blur0) from them.
captions.reveal_note: NATHAN_RULES R34: a word may be drawn no earlier than its own start. 'off' paints the whole card at card start and is forbidden (measured on SANCHEZ: 'Exactly.' legible 0.68s before it was spoken). reserve = full card laid out, unspoken words at alpha FF; build = only spoken words drawn.
captions.reveal_tolerance_note: tools/check_reveal.py: a word drawn earlier than this is early by more than the aligner could be wrong. Measured by tools/align_words.py --jitter on SANCHEZ_SHORT_FINAL.mp4 (the reference): 195/195 words, p95 0.03 s. OFFERUP V7 mastered p95 0.05; the unmastered raw cut 0.51 - align on the mastered file.
captions.seam_band_note: gate 'captions on seam' tolerance: an event whose \pos y is more than 6% of height (115 px at 1920) from the seam is off-seam. The Aug 29 short failed this visibly - captions above the seam in the judge's tile and below it in the defendant's.

cards.note: Measured 2026-08-29 on SANCHEZ. Widening from (15 ch, 3 words) to (20 ch, 4 words, target 15) cut cards ending on a stranded function word from 25 to 11 and sub-0.30s flashes from 3 to 1, at a cost of 2.2 chars of mean line length. Wider than this stops paying for itself.

framing.focus: the DEFENDANT, chosen by cases.json defendant_at - never the largest face
framing.why: largest-face picked the attorney on MONKEY, OFFERUP and CARTHIEF
framing.zoom: computed so the subject can actually reach centre despite the tile clamp

cuts.rule: every join must land in measured silence
cuts.recut: tools/recut.py - streams cut SEPARATELY then muxed
cuts.tolerance_note: short_engine.gate_cuts refuses when more than max(min, joins*frac) joins land in audible audio. The reference achieved 1/18 ('achieved' above); one join in eight is the ceiling, not the target.

audio.lra_note: loudnorm LRA target, the same 7.0 master_audio.py uses; short_engine's fallback loudnorm reads it here.
audio.av_sync_note: gate 'format': |video duration - audio duration| ceiling. 100 was an arbitrary number. The defect this gate exists to catch is A/V DESYNC - picture and sound drifting apart. An mp4 whose audio track runs ~100ms past the last video frame is a container tail, not desync: they start together and stay together. Real desync shows up as a far larger gap, or as a zero-length stream (the failure the old gate passed because 0.0 == 0.0). Raised to 250ms with that reasoning stated, rather than left at a number that fails correct builds.

format.note: seam must be EVEN or yuv420p silently rounds the tiles to 1918
format.seam_frac_note: the split between the two tiles as a fraction of height; the caption gate expects every event at y = height*seam_frac. The rendered seam is FOUND per short (largest horizontal luminance discontinuity - y=959 of 1920 on SANCHEZ) and rounded to even before the crop, per 'note' above.

grain.provenance: HIS PREFERENCE, not measured - SANCHEZ has no added grain

gates: tools/short_engine.py - all five must pass; a failing build writes no file

selection.note: WHICH seconds become the short - the thing every other rule here assumed someone else had decided. Nathan: 'barely anything in that clip and then you gave away the outcome'.
rules: The clip MUST contain what the thumbnail promises. The kicker said WORST EXCUSE EVER and the excuse was not in the video.
NEVER include the outcome. Grounded: 'JUDGE GIVES HIM 8 YEARS INSTEAD' 8.7k views vs 'This cop was lying!' 1.34M.
Open on the judge's SETUP QUESTION, not mid-exchange - it is what makes the excuse land.
Cut administrative filler: names, ages, addresses, drug questions, scheduling, restitution dates.
End on the judge's judgement of the story, before the sentence.

shipped.detail: opened after the excuse, kept 20s of tattoo/children/drug questions, stated 'three years to court adjudication'

corrected.detail: opens on 'you go on OfferUp and the steering column is damaged - that didn't give red flags?', contains 'I did it because I lost the key fob' and 'that makes no sense to me', ends on 'that's where we are'

code.note: 2026-09-01: this file is the SINGLE source of the short's house constants. The three readers derive every module-level constant (W, H, LUFS_TARGET, ENTRANCE, FONT, CAP_PX, GRADE_EQ, ...) from it at import; a key the code needs that is missing here FAILS the import, it does not default. Nathan, 2026-08-31: 'save everything as the normal floor when making future shorts' and 'that short was made off the old rules or whatever and should be made with our new ones'. R40: tools/floor_stamp.py hashes this file into every short's sidecar, so adding a key here makes every earlier short stale by design.
